evidence: Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8.10.3: haec causa prīmōs mēnsēs occupābit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a task that takes up time or attention; its first sense is to seize (see occupy-seize).

terms.grammar: adjective (participle of occupō); with in + ablative
evidence: Cic. Sen. 32: nēmō … cui fuerim occupātus
Cic. Off. 1.57: in patriā dēlendā occupātī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Busy with something is in aliquā rē occupātus. The opposite is ōtiōsus, at leisure (Cic. Tusc. 1.5); for “free, not busy” see available.

evidence: Cic. Inv. 2.132: in aliēnīs negōtiīs dētinērī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly to hold back or detain; then to keep someone occupied.
Busy with affairs and work; also of a thing that gives much work (prōvincia negōtiōsa, Cic. Mur. 18).

terms.gloss: be tied up, held up (by business)
terms.grammar: passive of impediō, impedīre, impedīvī, impedītum, to shackle
evidence: Auct. Her. 1.1: negōtiīs familiāribus impedītī (Lewis & Short s.v. familiāris)
terms.comment: Literally “to have one’s feet caught”: in- and pēs.

terms.gloss: be busy, have one’s hands full
evidence: Petr. 58.9: satagis tamquam mūs in matellā (Lewis & Short s.v. satis)
terms.comment: Written satis agere or sat agere in older Latin: “to have enough to do, have one’s hands full” (Lewis & Short s.v. satis); in Quintilian and Petronius, to bustle about.

phrases.latin: itaque nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit, cui fuerim occupātus
phrases.english: and so far no one has wanted to see me and found me busy

phrases.latin: Nihil mē interpellāstī, nōn enim occupātus eram.
phrases.english: You didn’t interrupt me at all: I wasn’t busy.
to be overwhelmed with work, as by a wave

phrases.latin: Quid crās agis? — Crās occupātus sum; perendiē vacābō.
phrases.english: What are you doing tomorrow? — I’m busy tomorrow; I’ll be free the day after.

phrases.latin: nōn domist, abiit ambulātum, dormit, ōrnātur, lavat, prandet, pōtat: occupātast, operae nōn est, nōn potest
phrases.english: she’s not at home, she’s gone for a walk, she’s asleep, she’s dressing, she’s in the bath, she’s at lunch, she’s drinking: she’s busy, she has no time, she can’t

phrases.latin: Quid negōtī est? nam occupātus sum ampliter.
phrases.english: What’s the matter? For I’m very busy.
